Content: “Scholars have been mesmerized by the huge extent of the present distribution of Bantu languages and could think of only a `text(single)` process, an equally huge human migration, 'the Bantu expansion,' to explain it... [This] scenario is fatally flawed, however, for two reasons. First it fell prey to the illusion that only a migration could fit the evidence... [But] a language can spread without involving the migration of any communities. The `text(second)` fatal error was to collapse a history which encompassed the developments of one to several millennia into a `text(single)` migration event. The evidence shows that many different dispersals of `text(single)` languages succeeded each other at different times, not continuously.”
